Container.Name: Tinyfin
Container.Overview: Jellyfin-compatible media server in one Go binary: same API and same clients, with all state in a single SQLite file instead of an in-memory catalog. WebUI and jellyfin-ffmpeg are included.
Container.Changes: Dropped the legacy Networking/Data/Environment blocks: they duplicate the Config entries, and a recreate that reads them came up with an empty environment and an invalid port binding on 17/nov. Initial template. Image 0.2.0.
Container.License: MIT (the image bundles the GPL-2.0 jellyfin-web build)
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: jellyfin media server movies tv shows transcode ffmpeg nvenc emby alternative
Container.Description:
Tinyfin speaks the Jellyfin HTTP API, so unchanged Jellyfin clients work against it: the web UI, the mobile and TV apps, the Kodi add-on, Findroid, Infuse. It is a clean-room implementation, not a fork, and the state lives in one SQLite file.
### First start
1. Open `http://<server>:8096/web/` and finish the first-run wizard. Create the admin user there before you expose the port. 2. Add libraries pointing at `/media`. The path is mounted read-only on purpose, because Tinyfin never writes to your files. 3. Reaching it from a Jellyfin client: use `http://<server>:8096` as the server address.
### Metadata and scanning
`TINYFIN_TMDB_API_KEY` is optional. Without it the scan catalogues files and reads local NFO and artwork, with no online metadata. The scanner skips a file when size and mtime did not change; `TINYFIN_SCAN_FORCE_PROBE` re-probes everything.
### Container notes
- The image is distroless: no shell, no curl, no wget. It cannot carry a Docker healthcheck. Check `GET /System/Info/Public` from outside instead. - The image runs as uid 65532 by default. The template adds `--user 99:100` so appdata stays `nobody:users` like every other Unraid container. Files created under `/data` belong to `nobody:users`. - `/data` holds `tinyfin.db`, `tinyfin.db.images`, `tinyfin.db.server-id` and `log/`. Keep it on a path you back up. A fresh instance starts empty. - NVIDIA hardware transcoding: add `--runtime=nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,video,utility` to the extra parameters and install the Unraid NVIDIA driver plugin. - The container port is 8096, the Jellyfin default, so a client only needs the new address. If Jellyfin or Emby already owns 8096 on this server, pick another host port.
### Status
Release `0.x`. Phases 0 to 3 are done and were tested against real clients. Coverage is honest, not complete: check `docs/COVERAGE.md` in the project before you rely on a feature. Live TV, DVR, DLNA, offline mobile sync and a plugin loader are out of scope for 0.x.
### Licensing
Tinyfin is MIT. This image also ships the GPL-2.0 `jellyfin-web` build as static files. The API-only variant with no bundled UI is published as the `Tinyfin API` template.
Project documentation: https://github.com/rafaelvieiras/tinyfin

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: HTTP port for the API and the bundled web UI. Jellyfin clients use the same port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: SQLite database, generated images, server id and logs. Keep it on a path you back up.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Your media, read-only. Libraries inside Tinyfin are added with the /media path.

Config.Name: TMDB API key
Config.Description: Enables online metadata. Empty: catalog-only scan using local NFO and artwork.

Config.Name: Scan concurrency
Config.Description: Scan workers per library. Raise it for a slow remote filesystem.

Config.Name: Library parallelism
Config.Description: Libraries scanned at the same time.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Container timezone for log timestamps. Empty: UTC.
